who we contact first and which channel f.text:
Harbor & Vale Retention Playbook > Who we contact first
Retention outreach is ranked by the churn model's risk score. Contact customers in this order:
1. Customers with a risk score of 0.70 or higher, newest first.
2. Customers who filed a complaint in the last month, whatever their score.
3. Customers with a risk score between 0.40 and 0.70.
Customers below 0.40 receive no individual outreach; they stay in the regular newsletter.

Harbor & Vale Retention Playbook > Channels
- High risk (0.70 and above): phone call by a retention agent.
- Medium risk (0.40 to 0.70): app push notification, then email after 2 days without response.
- Never contact the same customer more than twice in 14 days.

Harbor & Vale Retention Playbook > New customers (tenure 0 to 1 months)
New customers churn far more often than established ones. Every new customer flagged by the
model gets a welcome call within 3 days of the flag, plus a first-order follow-up email asking
whether delivery and payment went smoothly. Do not offer a discount on the first contact:
first fix the experience, then offer an incentive if the customer is still at risk a week later.

Exploratory Data Analysis Insights for Harbor & Vale Retention Team > Budget Implications
- Focus discount budget on customers using "Phone" as login device and those paying with "COD" payment mode, as these groups have the highest churn rates.
- The "Mobile" and "Mobile Phone" order categories also show very high churn and could be targeted for retention incentives.
- Single customers have a high churn rate (26.73%) and may benefit from targeted retention efforts.
- Missing data groups with high churn rates (e.g., missing Tenure or WarehouseToHome) might indicate customers with incomplete profiles who are at risk; consider outreach or data enrichment.
- Groups with similar category names but different churn rates (e.g., COD vs Cash on Delivery) should be treated separately in budget allocation due to their differing churn behaviors.

New customers churn far more often than established ones. Every new customer flagged by the
model gets a welcome call within 3 days of the flag, plus a first-order follow-up email asking
whether delivery and payment went smoothly. Do not offer a discount on the first contact:
first fix the experience, then offer an incentive if the customer is still at risk a week later.

Harbor & Vale Retention Campaign Results, Last Two Quarters > Campaign "Welcome Back" (new customers)
- Target: customers in their first two months, flagged by the model.
- Offer: welcome call plus a free-delivery voucher on the second order.
- Result: churn in the treated group was 9 percentage points lower than in the holdout.
- Lesson: the call mattered more than the voucher; customers who only got the voucher by email
  showed almost no uplift.

Competitor Offers Tracker > CartNest
- Positioning: low prices on electronics, especially phones and laptops.
- Current offer: 10% off the first phone order for new customers, paid as instant discount.
- Threat to us: high for customers whose preferred category is Mobile or Mobile Phone.

Harbor & Vale Retention Campaign Results, Last Two Quarters > Campaign "Sorry We Missed" (complaints)
- Target: customers with a complaint in the last month.
- Offer: coupon of INR 250 sent the same day as the complaint.
- Result: no improvement over the holdout; churn was slightly higher among customers whose
  complaint was still open when the coupon arrived.
- Lesson: this campaign led to the "resolve before you reward" rule in the playbook.

cash on delivery customers cashback free.text:
Harbor & Vale Retention Playbook > Cash on delivery (COD) customers
COD customers cannot be reached with wallet cashback, because they pay at the door. For them
use free-delivery vouchers or a small discount printed on the next invoice. Encourage, but never
require, a switch to UPI or a card.

Harbor & Vale Discount and Retention Budget Policy > Offers that need extra care
- Free delivery vouchers are preferred for cash on delivery customers.
- Do not offer discounts in the Grocery category: its churn is already low and margins are thin.
- Offers to customers with a risk score below 0.40 are not funded from this budget.

Harbor & Vale Retention Campaign Results, Last Two Quarters > Campaign "Wallet Boost" (cashback)
- Target: medium-risk customers paying by UPI or E wallet.
- Offer: INR 150 cashback on the next order above INR 1,000.
- Result: 3 percentage points lower churn than the holdout; cost per retained customer was high.
- Lesson: cashback works for wallet users but is wasted on COD customers, who cannot use it.

Harbor & Vale Discount and Retention Budget Policy > Limits per customer
- Maximum discount per customer per month: INR 500 or 15% of the next order, whichever is lower.
- Cashback offers are capped at INR 300 per customer per month and are paid to the wallet.
- A customer may receive at most one retention offer per 30 days.

Harbor & Vale Discount and Retention Budget Policy > Approval levels
- Up to INR 300: the retention agent decides.
- INR 301 to 500: team lead approval in the CRM.
- Above INR 500: not allowed for retention; escalate to the Head of Customer Experience.

Harbor & Vale Discount and Retention Budget Policy > Offers that need extra care
- Free delivery vouchers are preferred for cash on delivery customers.
- Do not offer discounts in the Grocery category: its churn is already low and margins are thin.
- Offers to customers with a risk score below 0.40 are not funded from this budget.

Harbor & Vale Discount and Retention Budget Policy > Monthly retention budget
The retention budget is INR 1,200,000 per month. It is split as follows:
- 50% for high-risk customers (risk score 0.70 and above)
- 30% for medium-risk customers (0.40 to 0.70)
- 20% reserve for complaint recovery, released by the support lead

Unused budget does not roll over to the next month.

Harbor & Vale Retention Playbook > Customers who complained
A complaint in the last month is the strongest single warning sign we track. The rule is
"resolve before you reward": a support agent closes the complaint first, and only then may the
retention team offer a coupon. A coupon sent while the complaint is still open is treated as an
apology for nothing and usually increases churn.

Harbor & Vale Retention Campaign Results, Last Two Quarters > Campaign "Sorry We Missed" (complaints)
- Target: customers with a complaint in the last month.
- Offer: coupon of INR 250 sent the same day as the complaint.
- Result: no improvement over the holdout; churn was slightly higher among customers whose
  complaint was still open when the coupon arrived.
- Lesson: this campaign led to the "resolve before you reward" rule in the playbook.

use free-delivery vouchers or a small discount printed on the next invoice. Encourage, but never
require, a switch to UPI or a card.
